messages.content: Write a self-contained fable of exactly 150 words about two parrots who disagree about sharing credit. Output no title or preamble. Include the final one-sentence moral in the 150-word total. Before responding, silently revise the draft until the entire response is between 140 and 170 words.

text:
The mango tree held two parrots who had painted the sky together, or so they claimed. Green said, "The sunset was my idea." Red snapped, "I flapped the clouds into place!" Their squabbling shook ripe fruit loose, which tumbled past a patient tortoise below.

"Who painted that?" the tortoise asked, pointing at a spiderweb strung with dew.

"We did," both parrots said instantly, in unison.

"Strange," the tortoise mused. "You argue over credit for clouds, yet share credit for a spider's work."

The parrots blinked. Green shifted on his branch. Red preened awkwardly. Neither could explain why claiming the sunset felt urgent, but claiming the web felt wrong.

"Perhaps," Green offered slowly, "we only fight over things we didn't truly make."

"Or things we fear we didn't," Red added.

That evening they split a mango, each crediting the tree.

A shared lie reveals more truth than a disputed truth ever will.
